messages.subject: Model Averaging in occupancy models
parts:
Hello all,

 

I was wondering what kind of model averaging unmarked applies in the fitlist command.

 

Also, I’m doing shrinkage model averaging  with the AICmodavg package on my beta estimates of my occupancy models. I noticed that AICmodavg notes mention:  “The shrinkage version of model averaging is only appropriate for cases where each parameter is given an equal weighting in the model (i.e., each parameter must appear the same number of times in the models) and has the same interpretation across all models”. So my question is: Is this limitation of the method by itself or only of the AICmodavg package?

 

I read  Luckas  et al. 2010: “Model selection bias and Freedman's paradox” and I didn’t find any paragraph where they mentioned this limitation.

I really appreciated any help.

 

 

Regards!

Alex

messages.author: 4e956cc50ac3e075
messages.subject: RE:[unmarked] Model Averaging in occupancy models
parts:
Hi Alejandro,

the statement regarding model-averaging beta estimates using the shrinkage estimator is a limit of the method. You should be careful when model-averaging beta estimates using any estimator. A beta estimate of a variable appearing in a model that also involves the same variable in an interaction (i.e., polynomial effects or other interactions) is not directly comparable to a beta estimate appearing in a model without such effects. This is one reason why some avoid model-averaging beta estimates and focus on real estimates instead, such as effect sizes (see ?modavgEffect).

Hope it helps,

Marc
